content.title: Denver, Wisconsin win Frozen Four games, to play for national title
content.text: Kyle Chyzowski of the Denver Pioneers celebrates with teammates after scoring a goal against the Michigan Wolverines during the Division I Men's Ice Hockey Championship held at T-Mobile Arena on April 9, 2026 in Las Vegas, Nevada.Tyler Schank/NCAA Photos via Getty Images Frozen Four semifinal scores: Denver outlasts No. 1 Michigan 4-3 in 2OT, Wisconsin beats North Dakota 2-1 The Frozen Four semifinals in the 2026 men’s hockey NCAA Tournament got underway Thursday in Las Vegas, and they did not disappoint as Wisconsin and Denver both won thrillers to advance to Saturday's championship game.Article continues below this adThe highlight was an instant classic in the nightcap between Denver and top-seeded Michigan that saw the Pioneers win 4-3 in double overtime. Denver twice erased one-goal deficits, including a game-tying goal from Clarke Caswell with 2:46 left in the third period. After a scoreless first overtime, Denver captain Kent Anderson rifled a shot past Michigan goalie Jack Ivankovic with 7:25 left in the second extra session to send the Pioneers into Saturday's championship game. Get Digital Access and Stay Informed With Trusted Local News.Get Digital Access and Stay Informed With Trusted Local News.ONLY 25¢Denver goalie Johnny Hicks turned in an incredible performance with 49 saves to backstop the win.Earlier in the night, Wisconsin scored a victory in its first Frozen Four appearance since 2010 as the Badgers knocked off No. 2 overall seed North Dakota 2-1. Simon Tassy and Ryan Botterill scored 27 seconds apart in the first period to spot the Badgers to an early lead, and Wisconsin survived a late comeback attempt from North Dakota to win on the shoulders of a stellar goaltending performance from Daniel Hauser. How to watch the Frozen Four championship game Denver and Wisconsin will meet in the national championship game on Sunday at 5:30 p.m. The game will air on ESPN.Article continues below this adMake the Times Union a Preferred Source on Google to see more of our journalism when you search.Add Preferred SourceDenver is seeking its record 11th national title, and is looking to claim the championship for the third time in the last five years. Wisconsin is looking to win a seventh national championship, though the Badgers haven't finished a season on top since 2006.A general view of the T-Mobile Arena before the first game of the NCAA Division I Men's Ice Hockey Frozen Four semifinal at the T-Mobile Arena on April 9, 2026 in Las Vegas, Nevada.Richard T Gagnon/Getty Images Frozen Four semifinal live updates: Denver vs. Michigan hockey Michigan and Denver met in the night's second semifinal. Denver won and will play in the final against Wisconsin. The Times Union provided updates throughout the game.Article continues below this ad Final: Denver 4, Michigan 3 (2OT) Denver wins instant classic 4-3 on Kent Anderson goal 12:51 a.m.: Kent Anderson is the hero, and Denver is heading to the national championship game.With 7:25 left in the second overtime, Anderson drifted into the slot from his spot on the right point and ripped a shot past Michigan's Jack Ivankovic for the winner to send Denver into Saturday's final.Article continues below this adIt's just the second goal of the year for Anderson. Kristian Epperson and Eric Jamieson had the assists. Michigan, Denver showing wear and tear in 2OT 12:45 a.m.: Past the midway point of the second overtime, Michigan and Denver are still tied 3-3 at T-Mobile Arena.Michigan has dominated in terms of shots on goal, outshooting Denver 13-2 so far in the second overtime and 52-25 for the game, but the Wolverines have been unable to get the winner past Denver's Johnny Hicks, who has 49 saves.Article continues below this adMost of the second overtime has consisted of long-distance shots and pucks being dumped into the zone by tiring teams. Michigan vs. Denver: 2OT begins 12:26 a.m.: The puck has dropped for the second overtime at T-Mobile Arena in Las Vegas.Next goal wins between Michigan and Denver, who are tied 3-3 through 80 minutes in the second of two national semifinals. Kyle Chyzowski, Cale Ashcroft and Clarke Caswell have the goals for Denver, while Josh Eernisse, TJ Hughes and Jayden Perron have scored for Michigan.Article continues below this adMichigan has a little less than 30 seconds of power play time remaining as the second OT begins. End 1st OT: Michigan 3, Denver 3 What are the longest games in Frozen Four history? 12:17 a.m.: For the second straight season, Denver is playing a Frozen Four game that will head to a second overtime.Article continues below this adIn the 2025 national semifinals, the Pioneers fell 4-3 in double overtime to eventual national champion Western Michigan. Michigan was involved in the longest Frozen Four game in history, a three-overtime loss to Maine on March 30, 1995 in Providence, R.I.The longest game in the history of the NCAA Tournament was on March 27, 2021, when Minnesota Duluth beat North Dakota 4-3 in five overtimes in Fargo, N.D. in a regional final. That game took 142 minutes and 13 seconds before a winner was decided. Michigan, Denver will head to double OT 12:10 a.m.: Turns out that 80 minutes wasn't enough to settle things between Michigan and Denver in the Frozen Four semifinals, either.Article continues below this adAfter a tense 20 minutes of overtime with both teams generating chances, neither team was able to net the golden goal. We'll get a second overtime at T-Mobile Arena in Las Vegas. Power play ends with Denver penalty 12:08 a.m.: Denver couldn't convert on a power play that only lasted for 54 seconds, because the Pioneers committed a penalty of their own.Sam Harris is called for tripping with 1:31 left in the first overtime. If this one heads to a second overtime, Michigan will have a brief man advantage at the start of that period.Article continues below this ad Power play for Denver 12:02 a.m.: With 2:26 left in overtime, Denver is going to get a golden opportunity to try and win this one.Michigan's Will Horcoff is called for a two-minute slashing minor, and the Pioneers will get their fifth power play of the night. Denver was 0-for-4 with the man advantage in regulation.Denver is without one of its best power play options, Boston Buckberger, who came off the ice with a bleeding hand a few minutes ago.Article continues below this ad Denver nearly wins it 11:51 p.m.: Michigan has controlled most of this overtime session, but Denver just came the closest yet to winning it.Clarke Caswell, who scored the tying goal late in the third period, threw a pass in front of the net that Rieger Lorenz deflected. The shot got over the left shoulder of Michigan goalie Jack Ivankovic, but the puck hit the crossbar and went out of play to keep things tied with 8:15 left in the first OT. Tension building in Michigan vs. Denver OT 11:46 p.m.: Both teams have generated chances, but as they break to shovel the ice midway through the 20-minute overtime period, we've had no breakthrough.Article continues below this adMichigan has a 5-2 advantage in shots on goal during this overtime, but Denver goalie Johnny Hicks has stood tall, including a stellar save on Garrett Schifsky. Hicks has 33 saves so far tonight. Michigan goalie Jack Ivankovic has 17 stops. TJ Hughes slow getting to Michigan bench 11:35 p.m.: It's a scary moment for Michigan early in overtime as star senior TJ Hughes skates slowly to the bench, favoring his right arm and shoulder.Hughes is a finalist for the Hobey Baker Award, which will be handed out Friday night. He has 22 goals and 35 assists this season, including Michigan's second goal tonight.Article continues below this adThankfully for Michigan, Hughes is able to return to the ice for his next shift. Overtime begins in Michigan vs. Denver 11:30 p.m.: Michigan vs. Denver. Next goal wins.The puck has dropped in overtime in a 3-3 game in the Frozen Four.Article continues below this adMichigan is playing its fifth overtime game this season. The Wolverines are 4-0-1 in games that have gone beyond 60 minutes, and won the shootout with Penn State in their lone game that finished in a tie after overtime.Denver is in overtime for the 11th time this season. The Pioneers are 4-3-3 in overtime games this season, with two shootout losses and one shootout win.There won’t be any shootouts tonight. They’re playing until somebody scores a winning goal. End 3rd: Michigan 3, Denver 3 Michigan, Denver have Frozen Four OT history 11:20 p.m.: This is the second-ever meeting between Denver and Michigan at the Frozen Four, and both have gone to overtime.Article continues below this adIn 2022, the Wolverines and Pioneers also played in the national semifinals when the Frozen Four was played in Boston. Denver was victorious on that occasion, winning 3-2 on a rebound goal by Carter Savoie with 5:07 left in overtime. Denver went on to beat Minnesota State for the 2022 national title. Michigan and Denver going to OT tied 3-3 11:14 p.m.: Sixty minutes in Las Vegas won't be enough to settle things in the semifinal between Michigan and Denver in the Frozen Four.Article continues below this adTied 2-2 after two periods, Michigan took the lead on the power play with 8:58 to play on Jayden Perron's 18th goal of the year, but Clarke Caswell's eighth goal of the year allowed Denver to tie it up with 2:46 to play.It'll be sudden death OT to determine who plays Wisconsin in Saturday's championship game. Denver's Clarke Caswell ties it at 3-3 11:10 p.m.: Buckle up, we're in for a wild finish as Denver's Clarke Caswell has tied it at 3-3 with 2:46 to play.Article continues below this adCaswell, one of a number of standout freshmen for the Pioneers, parks himself in the crease and scores to knot things up in Las Vegas once again. Garrett Brown and Kristian Epperson had the assists on Caswell's eighth goal of the season. Jayden Perron gives Michigan a 3-2 lead 10:58 p.m.: After finally getting a power play opportunity, Michigan didn't waste time taking the 3-2 lead.Jayden Perron nets the go-ahead goal for Michigan with 8:58 left in the third period, ripping a shot past Johnny Hicks from the high slot.Article continues below this adIt's the 18th goal of the season for Perron, a 21-year-old from Winnipeg. Will Horcoff and Malcolm Spence assisted on the goal. Michigan goes on the power play 10:55 p.m.: For the first time tonight, Michigan's top-ranked power play unit will get a chance.With 9:46 left in a 2-2 game in the third period, Denver's Eric Jamieson is called for a two-minute boarding minor.Article continues below this adThe Wolverines' man-up unit, led by TJ Hughes, Will Horcoff and Michael Hage, has scored 43 goals in 136 opportunities this season, an NCAA-best 31.6% success rate. Power plays piling up for Denver hockey 10:47 p.m.: A boarding penalty on Michigan's Garrett Schifsky results in Denver getting its fourth power play of the night.Denver came up empty on its first three chances with the man advantage tonight, all of which came courtesy of penalties on Michigan defenseman Tyler Duke.Article continues below this adMichigan, which boasts the top power play unit in college hockey, has yet to get a power play tonight. Scary collision leaves Denver's Johnny Hicks down 10:42 p.m.: Denver goalie Johnny Hicks is slow to get up after a scary collision with Michigan forward Malcolm Spence, who tumbled into Hicks while charging in on goal.Denver and Michigan are still tied 2-2 with 16:07 to play after Michigan successfully killed off a penalty for the third time tonight.Article continues below this adHicks remains in the game after being looked at by the Denver training staff. No penalty was called, nor was there a challenge for contact to the head. 3rd period begins between Denver and Michigan hockey 10:35 p.m.: We’ve got 20 minutes left in regulation in the second semifinal of tonight’s Frozen Four action in Las Vegas. Denver and Michigan start the third period tied at 2-2.Denver scored first on a Kyle Chyzowski goal in the first period, with Michigan answering on goals from Josh Eernisse and Hobey Baker Award finalist TJ Hughes to make it 2-1 after the opening period. Denver tied it up early in the second period on Cole Ashcroft’s third goal of the season.Article continues below this ad End 2nd period: Michigan 2, Denver 2 Who is Denver goalie Johnny Hicks? 10:28 p.m.: Freshman Johnny Hicks started the season as Denver’s No. 3 goaltender and didn’t get his first start until Jan. 24. So far, he’s yet to lose a college hockey game.Hicks, a 5-foot-10 native of Kamloops, British Columbia, is 14-0-1 this season with a 1.12 goals against average, an NCAA-leading .958 save percentage and three shutouts. He’s only allowed more than two goals in a game once, when Minnesota Duluth put three goals past him on March 21 in the final of the NCHC Frozen Faceoff — a game Denver won 4-3 in double overtime.Article continues below this adHicks has made 20 saves through the first two periods tonight. Michigan, Denver hockey deadlocked after 2nd period 10:20 p.m.: After 40 minutes in Las Vegas, it's all tied at 2-2 between Denver and Michigan in the Frozen Four to see which team advances to face Wisconsin in Saturday's national championship game.Denver scored the second period's only goal, a wrist shot from the point by Cale Ashcroft 2:30 into the second that tied things up. Michigan had taken a 2-1 lead after one period with goals from Josh Eernisse and TJ Hughes following the opener from Denver's Kyle Chyzowski.Article continues below this adMichigan has a 22-15 lead in shots on goal through two periods. Michigan’s destiny vs. Denver’s dynasty 10:08 p.m.: Both Michigan and Denver are storied hockey programs, but one is trying to end a long run of tournament disappointments while the other is trying to continue a recent run of dominance.Michigan has won nine NCAA championships, with seven of them coming between 1948 and 1964, but after winning titles in 1996 and 1998, the Wolverines have come up blank since then despite this being their 10th Frozen Four appearance since their most recent title.Article continues below this adDenver has an NCAA record 10 national titles, and is looking for its third championship in the last five years. The Pioneers were the last team standing in 2022 and 2024, and are making their third straight Frozen Four appearance and fourth in the last five years. Denver's Cale Ashcroft ties it up 9:45 p.m.: We're tied up at 2-2 2:30 into the second period.Just like with Denver's first goal, the Pioneers' second comes shortly after a power play expires. Cale Ashcroft fires home a long wrist shot from the point through a screen of defenders. It's Ashcroft's third goal of the season, with Sam Harris and Clarke Caswell providing the assists for the Pioneers.Article continues below this ad Denver, Michigan hockey start 2nd period in Vegas 9:40 p.m.: The second period is underway between Michigan and Denver in tonight’s second semifinal in Las Vegas.Michigan leads 2-1 after the opening 20 minutes, as the Wolverines answered the opening goal from Denver’s Kyle Chyzowski with tallies from Josh Eernisse and TJ Hughes.Michigan, the No. 1 overall seed in the tournament, is looking to end a championship drought that dates back to 1998.Article continues below this ad End 1st period: Michigan 2, Denver 1 Who is Michigan hockey’s TJ Hughes? 9:31 p.m.: While he’s not related to Olympic gold medal-winning brothers Jack and Quinn Hughes, Michigan’s TJ Hughes is accomplished in his own right.The 2025-26 Big Ten Player of the Year and a Hobey Baker Award finalist, Hughes is the NCAA’s active career leader with 69 goals, 110 assists and 179 points over his four years playing for the Wolverines.Article continues below this adWith his go-ahead goal in tonight’s first period, Hughes — a 6-foot native of Hamilton, Ontario — has 22 goals and 35 assists so far this season. Michigan hockey leads Denver after first period 9:24 p.m.: After a frenetic first 20 minutes in Las Vegas, Michigan has a 2-1 lead against Denver.Denver struck first on a Kyle Chyzowski goal just before the midway point of the first period, but Michigan answered with two goals a minute apart late in the period. Josh Eernisse scored the first, and Hobey Baker Award finalist TJ Hughes scored the second.Article continues below this adShots on goal favored Denver, 10-9, in the opening period. TJ Hughes puts Michigan up 2-1 9:20 p.m.: After Josh Eernisse tied it for Michigan, it took just 59 seconds for Michigan to take the lead as TJ Hughes knocks one in from just outside the crease.It's the 22nd goal of the season for Hughes, a Hobey Baker Award finalist and the active NCAA career leader in both goals and assists. Adam Valentini and Michael Hage provided the assists. It's the NCAA-best 39th assist of the season for Hage.Article continues below this ad Michigan's Josh Eernisse makes it 1-1 9:19 p.m.: We're all tied up late in the first period in Las Vegas as Josh Eernisse rips the tying shot past Denver goalie Johnny Hicks with 3:42 left in the second period.It's the 11th goal of the season for Eernisse, a 24-year-old senior from Eagan, Minn. Kienan Draper, the son of former Detroit Red Wings standout Kris Draper, recorded the assist. Denver leads 1-0 on Kyle Chyzowski goal 9:03 p.m.: It's Denver that's on the board first in tonight's second semifinal.Article continues below this adShortly after Denver was held scoreless on a power play, the Pioneers strike first as a Michigan turnover results in a slick passing play. Kyle Chyzowski fires home his 12th goal of the year with 10:31 left in the opening period. Brendan McMorrow and Kieran Cebrian provided the assists. Denver, Michigan hockey underway in Frozen Four 8:46 p.m.: The puck has dropped at T-Mobile Arena, and Michigan and Denver are underway in tonight’s second semifinal. The winner will face Wisconsin in the NCAA championship game on Saturday.Coach David Carle’s Denver team is 14-0-1 in its last 15 games and is led by Hobey Baker Award finalist Eric Pohlkamp with 18 goals and Clarke Caswell with 25 assists.Article continues below this adCoach Brandon Naurato’s Michigan squad is the No. 1 overall seed for the tournament and is seeking the program’s first national title since 1998. Will Horcoff is the Wolverines’ top goalscorer with 25, while Michael Hage has a team-high 38 assists. Hobey Baker finalist TJ Hughes has 56 points on 21 goals and 35 assists.Denver is 27-11-3 entering tonight’s contest, while Michigan has a 31-7-1 record on the season. Michigan seeking historic basketball, hockey double 8:33 p.m.: No school has ever won NCAA championships in men’s basketball and men’s hockey in the same year. Michigan has a chance to break that barrier this season.Article continues below this adMichigan basketball, coached by Dusty May led by Final Four Most Oustanding Player Elliot Cadeau, Morez Johnson Jr., Aday Mara and Yaxel Lendeborg, beat UConn 69-63 in the national championship game on Monday night in Indianapolis.Michigan hockey is two wins away from a title of its own and a piece of college sports history. Previewing Michigan vs. Denver hockey 8:10 p.m.: Michigan and Denver, the two programs with the most NCAA hockey championships, will face off at 8:45 p.m. to see who heads to Saturday’s national title game against WisconsinArticle continues below this adMichigan, the No. 1 overall seed in this year’s tournament, has won nine NCAA titles, but is seeking to end a championship drought that runs back to 1998. The Wolverines, led by senior forward TJ Hughes and freshman goaltender Jack Ivankovic, are making their record 29th Frozen Four appearance after beating Bentley and Minnesota Duluth to get through the Albany Regional.Denver, owner of an NCAA-record 10 national titles, comes into Las Vegas on a hot streak with a 14-0-1 record over its last 15 games. The Pioneers claimed the shootout win following the lone tie in that streak. Denver powered to the Loveland Regional title with a 5-0 win over Cornell and a 6-2 win against Western Michigan.The four teams in this year’s Frozen Four are the four most decorated in terms of national championships: Denver (10), Michigan (9), North Dakota (8) and Wisconsin (6).“Everyone keeps talking about the four bluebloods, all the national championships,” Michigan coach Brandon Naurato said. “All three games are going to be sold out. It will be great for college hockey.”Article continues below this ad Frozen Four semifinal live updates: North Dakota vs. Wisconsin hockey North Dakota and Wisconsin met in the night's first semifinal. The Badgers were victorious and will face Denver in the championship game on Saturday. The Times Union provided updates throughout the game. Final: Wisconsin 2, North Dakota 1 Wisconsin hockey beats North Dakota to advance to championship game 7:43 p.m.: It’s “On Wisconsin” to Saturday’s NCAA championship game.Article continues below this adFreshman goalie Daniel Hauser turned in a spectacular performance, finishing with 21 saves, as Wisconsin hockey beat North Dakota 2-1 in the first of two NCAA Frozen Four semifinal games in Las Vegas.Wisconsin got two goals in quick succession in the first period, with Simon Tassy and Ryan Botterill scoring 27 seconds apart, and Hauser’s sensational play in goal was enough to make it hold up, even with North Dakota’s Ellis Rickwood making it a one-goal game in the final minute.Jan Spunar finished with 35 saves for North Dakota.Wisconsin will face the winner of tonight’s second semifinal between Michigan and Denver in Saturday’s championship game.Article continues below this ad North Dakota hockey finally scores 7:40 p.m.: It took into the final minute of regulation, but North Dakota is finally on the board as Ellis Rickwood scores to make it a 2-1 game with 51.8 seconds left in the third period.With North Dakota's goalie pulled for an extra attacker, the numbers pay off for the Fighting Hawks as Rickwood scores his ninth goal of the season by converting a scramble in front of the net. Dylan James and Ben Strinden had the assists. Wisconsin hockey’s penalty kill shining 7:17 p.m.: Wisconsin’s penalty kill entered tonight ranking just 62nd in NCAA Division I hockey, but the Badgers’ man-down unit is shining tonight.Article continues below this adNorth Dakota had its fourth power play opportunity tonight after Wisconsin’s Luke Osburn was called for tripping, but the Badgers once again kept the Fighting Hawks off the board. Goalie Daniel Hauser is shining, he’s up to 19 saves and is looking for his fourth shutout of the season as Wisconsin still leads 2-0 midway through the third period. 20 minutes left for Wisconsin, North Dakota hockey 7 p.m.: The final period of regulation is underway between Wisconsin and North Dakota in the first of two Frozen Four semifinals at T-Mobile Arena in Las Vegas.Wisconsin claimed a 2-0 lead in the first period on goals 27 seconds apart from Simon Tassy and Ryan Botterill. North Dakota had multiple power play opportunities in the second period, including a lengthy 5-on-3, but couldn’t get a puck past Wisconsin goalie Daniel Hauser.Article continues below this ad End 2nd period: Wisconsin 2, North Dakota 0 Who is Wisconsin hockey goalie Daniel Hauser? 6:51 p.m.: All four starting goalies in this year’s Frozen Four are freshmen, and one of them, Wisconsin’s Daniel Hauser, has been spectacular so far tonight.Hauser, a 22-year-old from Chestermere, Alberta, came to Wisconsin this season after wrapping up his junior hockey career in the Western Hockey League, where he is the all-time career wins leader.Article continues below this adTonight is his 33rd appearance and 29th start of the season. Entering tonight, Hauser has a 20-7-2 record with three shutouts, a 2.56 goals against average and an .899 save percentage. Wisconsin hockey survives North Dakota surge in 2nd 6:43 p.m.: It wasn't easy to maintain it, but Wisconsin hockey still has a 2-0 lead on North Dakota through two periods in the first of two Frozen Four semifinals in Las Vegas.The Badgers survived three penalties during the second period, and kept North Dakota off the board for a 5-on-3 power play that took up nearly two minutes. A terrific backcheck by Oliver Tulk in the final minute helped deny North Dakota's Ollie Josephson, who had a breakaway opportunity against Wisconsin goalie Daniel Hauser.Article continues below this adNorth Dakota outshot Wisconsin 12-7 during the second period, though Wisconsin still has a 25-16 advantage in shots on goal for the game. North Dakota hockey getting 5-on-3 6:33 p.m.: North Dakota has been much more competitive this period, but hasn't been able to break through yet. Now, the Fighting Hawks are getting a prime opportunity.North Dakota has a 5-on-3 power play for a minute and 56 seconds with 6:19 left in the second after two penalties on Wisconsin just four seconds apart. Luke Osburn was called for holding and Joe Palodichuk was called for interference.Article continues below this ad Puck drops for second period 6:04 p.m.: The second period is underway in the first of tonight’s two Frozen Four semifinals in Las Vegas.Wisconsin’s Simon Tassy and Ryan Botterill scored goals 27 seconds apart to give the Badgers a 2-0 lead over North Dakota after the opening 20 minutes at T-Mobile Arena. North Dakota had not allowed a goal in this year’s NCAA Tournament until Tassy beat freshman goalie Jan Spunar with 7:06 left in the first.The Badgers outshot North Dakota 18-4 in the opening period and won 15-of-23 faceoffs.Article continues below this adRyan Botterill of the Wisconsin Badgers scores a goal against Jan Spunar of the North Dakota Fighting Hawks in the first period of a semifinal game of the NCAA Division I men's ice hockey championship at T-Mobile Arena on April 09, 2026 in Las Vegas, Nevada. Ethan Miller/Getty Images End 1st period: Wisconsin 2, North Dakota 0 All Wisconsin after 20 minutes 5:50 p.m.: After the first period of the first Frozen Four semifinal game at T-Mobile Arena, it's a 2-0 lead for Wisconsin over North Dakota.Article continues below this adThe Badgers got goals from Simon Tassy and Ryan Botterill 27 seconds apart to take control on the scoreboard. Wisconsin finished the first period with a massive 18-4 advantage in shots on goal, though the Badgers were unable to add to their lead despite a power play opportunity shortly after their two-goal outburst.North Dakota freshman goalie Jan Spunar allowed his first two goals of the NCAA Tournament, but he still came up with 16 saves in the opening period to keep things from getting out of hand.Ryan Botterill of the Wisconsin Badgers celebrates with teammates after scoring a goal during the first period against the North Dakota Fighting Hawks during the Division I Men's Ice Hockey Championship held at T-Mobile Arena on April 9, 2026 in Las Vegas, Nevada.Tyler Schank/NCAA Photos via Getty Images Wisconsin scores two goals in quick succession 5:35 p.m.: After dominating the first 13 minutes of the first period, Wisconsin has taken a 2-0 lead against North Dakota on two goals just 27 seconds apart.Article continues below this adSimon Tassy gave Wisconsin the breakthrough with 7:06 left in the first period, firing home a pass from Vasily Zelenov. It was Tassy's 14th goal of the year. Ryan Botterill quickly doubled the lead, scoring his 10th goal of the season. Ben Dexheimer and Joe Palodichuk had the assists.Those are the first two goals that North Dakota has allowed during the NCAA Tournament. Wisconsin controlling early action 5:26 p.m.: Just past the midway point of the opening period, it's still a 0-0 game, but Wisconsin has controlled the run of play.Article continues below this adThe Badgers have a 9-3 advantage in shots on goal, but have yet to put a puck past Jan Spunar. The North Dakota freshman goalie is on an incredible hot streak thanks to back-to-back shutouts in the Sioux Falls Regional, as the Fighting Hawks have not allowed a goal yet during this NCAA Tournament.Daniel Hauser, Wisconsin's freshman goalie, has only faced three shots but has already produced a couple of stellar saves from point-blank range. North Dakota, Wisconsin hockey underway in Frozen Four 5:06 p.m.: The puck has dropped, and North Dakota and Wisconsin are underway in tonight’s first semifinal from Las Vegas, where “hockey weather” is 85 degrees and sunny.Article continues below this adCoach Dane Jackson’s North Dakota team is led in scoring by Dylan James with 21 goals and Cole Reschny with 29 assists. Meanwhile, Wisconsin coach Mike Hastings' team has received 17 goals from Quinn Finley and 27 assists from Gavin Morrissey.Each team is seeking to win a national title in a program anniversary year. North Dakota last won the national championship 10 years ago in 2016. Meanwhile, Wisconsin won two decades ago in 2006. North Dakota brings a 29-9-1 record into today’s game and Wisconsin owns a 23-12-2 mark.Article continues below this ad Previewing North Dakota vs. Wisconsin hockey 4:15 p.m.: North Dakota and Wisconsin, a pair of programs making their returns to the Frozen Four after lengthy absences, will kick off tonight’s semifinal action in Las Vegas.North Dakota, the No. 2 overall seed for the NCAA Tournament, is back in the Frozen Four for the first time since winning the national championship in 2016. The Fighting Hawks were dominant in their run through the Sioux Falls Regional, beating Merrimack 3-0 and Quinnipiac 5-0.“We're obviously extremely excited to be back here,” North Dakota coach Dane Jackson said. “These guys have put in a lot of work all the way from summer training through July and August, a great training camp, then a consistent full season. The amount of buy-in, team-first kind of attitude from our players has been a real strength to our group.”Article continues below this adWisconsin is in the Frozen Four for the first time since 2010. The Badgers, the No. 12 seed in the 16-team tournament, earned their spot in Las Vegas with a thrilling win over Michigan State as Ben Dexheimer’s overtime goal gave Wisconsin a 4-3 win. Wisconsin’s regional semifinal win over Dartmouth was the program’s first NCAA Tournament victory since the 2010 Frozen Four semifinals.Jayden Perron of Michigan celebrates with his team after scoring a goal against Minnesota Duluth during the NCAA Regional Championship game at MVP Arena in Albany, NY on Sunday, March 29, 2026.Stephen Weaver How to watch the Frozen Four? What channel are the games on? Both semifinal games and the championship will be shown on ESPN2 and streamed on ESPN+.Article continues below this ad When is the Frozen Four national championship game? Thursday’s winners will play at 5:30 p.m. ET Saturday.That game will be available to watch on ESPN2 or ESPN+. NCAA hockey tournament 2026 bracket Teams advanced to this week’s action from games played in four regions.Article continues below this ad Albany, N.Y. winner: Michigan Loveland, Colo. winner: Denver Sioux Falls, S.D. winner: North Dakota Worcester, Mass. winner: Wisconsin Frozen Four team-by-team breakdown Some quick facts on each of this year’s national semifinalists.Article continues below this ad Michigan hockey Record: 31-7-1 Coach: Brandon Naurato Goals scored leader: Will Horcoff (25) Assists leader: Michael Hage (38) Conference: Big Ten North Dakota hockey Record: 29-9-1 Coach: Dane Jackson Goals scored leader: Dylan James (21) Assists leader: Cole Reschny (29) Conference: NCHC Article continues below this ad Denver hockey Record: 27-11-3 Coach: David Carle Goals scored leader: Eric Pohlkamp (18) Assists leader: Clarke Caswell (25) Conference: NCHC Wisconsin hockey Record: 23-12-2 Coach: Mike Hastings Goals scored leader: Quinn Finley (17) Assists leader: Gavin Morrissey (27) Conference: Big Ten Article continues below this ad Who will win this year’s Hobey Baker award? In between the Frozen Four’s semifinals and championship game, the Hobey Baker Memorial Award Foundation will announce this year’s winner of college hockey’s top individual prize. That award winner gets announced Friday during an 8 p.m. ET ceremony broadcast on NHL Network and streamed at hobeybaker.com.Two of the three finalists are playing in the Frozen Four. Hobey Baker finalists T.J Hughes, Michigan: The top player on the nation’s top team, Hughes has recorded 21 goals and 35 assists this season, and won 57.8% of his faceoffs. The Michigan captain was this year’s Big Ten Player of the Year and ranks No. 3 in the country in points per game at 1.44. Max Plante, Minnesota Duluth: Plante is the lone finalist whose season is complete. He scored 25 goals and dished 27 assists, and was named NCHC Player of the Year. Eric Pohlkamp, Denver: A high-scoring defenseman, Pohlkamp has registered 18 goals and 21 assists. The NCHC Offensive Defenseman of the Year set a conference goals record for a defenseman this season. Article continues below this ad Where are the 2026 Frozen Four games? This year’s Frozen Four takes place at T-Mobile Arena, which is in the town of Paradise right next to the city of Las Vegas.The arena, which opened in 2016, serves as the home ice of the NHL’s Vegas Golden Knights.
